title: Sync the tab title
prompt:
Two jobs in `Watchlist`:

1. **Remove the unnecessary Effect.** `left` is copied into state by an Effect. Calculate it during render instead.
2. **Sync the browser tab title.** While the Watchlist is on screen, `document.title` should read **2 to watch · Watchlist** (with the real number), and update when a movie is marked watched. When the Watchlist is removed (click **Hide watchlist**), the title must go back to what it was before, **Playground**.
hints: Replace the `left` state and its Effect with `const left = movies.filter((m) => !m.watched).length;`
The title Effect reads `left`, so its dependency array is `[left]`.
Save the old title inside the Effect (`const previous = document.title;`) and return a cleanup that puts it back.
explanation: `left` is derived from `movies`, so it's calculated during render. The Effect version rendered once with a wrong count of 0 and then again with the right one. The document title, on the other hand, lives outside React, so syncing it is a real Effect. Listing `[left]` re-runs it only when the count changes, and the cleanup restores the previous title both before each re-run and when the component unmounts. That's also exactly what StrictMode's mount, cleanup, mount check exercises in development.

checks.title-initial: The tab title is "2 to watch · Watchlist"
checks.title-updates: Marking Past Lives watched updates the title to "1 to watch · Watchlist"
checks.title-cleanup: Hiding the Watchlist restores the title "Playground"
